title: Highly Tunable Photon-Magnon Coupling Governed by Collective-Mode Profiles in Reconfigurable Dielectric-Resonator Arrays
authors: Shihao Zhou, Edward Kwao, Junming Wu, Abhijit Shinde, Yin Lyu, Rene Lopez, Wencan Jin, Yi Li, Binbin Yang, Wei Zhang
abstract: The spatial structure of a microwave photon mode provides a degree of freedom for controlling its interaction with a localized magnetic excitation. We demonstrate site-selective magnon-photon coupling in modular arrays of discrete dielectric resonators mounted on a common microstrip line. The resonators can be added, removed, or rearranged on the same completed PCB, enabling post-fabrication geometrical reconfiguration of the collective photon modes and their nodal structure. A YIG sphere is positioned successively above individual resonators, while an in-plane magnetic field tunes its Kittel mode through the collective photon resonances. In a three-resonator array, modes with finite local microwave magnetic fields hybridize with the magnon at every measured site, whereas a mode containing a central field node exhibits no resolvable splitting when the sphere is positioned at that node. Full-wave simulations and a coupled-mode model show that the interaction is governed by the local amplitude of the collective photon mode rather than by spectral resonance alone. Extending this local-node selection rule to a five-resonator array successfully predicts the measured position-dependent coupling patterns. These results establish post-fabrication control of spatial magnon-photon hybridization and provide a route toward reconfigurable magnonic interfaces in future hybrid quantum microwave architectures.
summary: This research demonstrates site-selective control over magnon-photon coupling in reconfigurable microwave circuits by exploiting the spatial profile of the collective photon mode. By physically reconfiguring dielectric resonators, the coupling strength can be tuned based on where the local magnetic field of the photon mode is non-zero. This establishes a powerful, programmable route for building hybrid quantum microwave devices.
main_problem: The paper addresses controlling the interaction between localized magnetic excitations (magnons) and microwave photons by exploiting the spatial structure of the photon mode.
main_result: The magnon-photon coupling is governed by the local amplitude of the collective photon mode at the magnon position, leading to a site-selective coupling rule that can be demonstrated and predicted in reconfigurable arrays.
method: The study combines full-wave electromagnetic simulations (HFSS) with coupled-mode modeling to analyze transmission spectra as a function of external magnetic field and resonator geometry.
model_or_system: The system uses modular arrays of dielectric resonators on a PCB to create tunable collective photon modes. The interaction is modeled by coupling the YIG magnon mode to these photon modes, whose collective behavior is described by nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian approximations.
key_observables: Site-selective magnon-photon coupling (observed as avoided crossings in transmission spectra), collective mode frequencies, and local microwave magnetic field profiles.
important_parameters: External magnetic field ($H_{ext}$), resonator separation ($d$), and the local amplitude of the collective photon mode.
main_assumptions: Initially, the ideal model assumes uniform nearest-neighbor coupling, but the authors note that real-world geometric asymmetry breaks this symmetry, requiring a more complex vector field treatment.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup, $S_{12}$ spectra for various resonator configurations (2-DR, 3-DR, 4-DR), and position-resolved coupling patterns demonstrating site-dependent hybridization.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from demonstrating site-selectivity in small arrays (3-DR) to establishing the general principle of local-node selection, and finally discussing the limitations of idealized models by analyzing larger, asymmetric arrays (4-DR).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, experimentally verifiable platform for engineering quantum light-matter interactions, moving beyond simple spectral matching to utilize the spatial wave function structure for control.

Spintronics.note: The core mechanism of site-selective magnon-photon coupling in a reconfigurable microwave circuit directly relates to the central theme of magnon/photon polaritons and hybrid spin-photon systems in spintronics.
